title: emir run (the run summary)
description: One run's results: what `--format json` prints and `--summary-out` writes. Screening, not sign-off (`disclaimer`); a research project, no guarantee of accuracy (`research_disclaimer`). `simulator_verification` says whether this machine verified the simulator that wrote the currents.

research_disclaimer.const: EMIR is a research project, provided as is, with no warranty or guarantee of accuracy. It is your responsibility to test and verify its results for your process, tools and design before relying on them.

simulator_verification.description: Whether the latest valid `emir verify-sim` record of this machine for the simulator, version, output format and simulator arguments that wrote the run's currents passed with this emir minor version (`verified`, EMIR-I463). `not verified` gives its `reason`: `no record` or `other host` or `stale` (a pass of another emir minor version) with EMIR-W464 and `command`, the verification to run; `failed` (the latest record failed: a later failure cancels an earlier pass) with EMIR-W414; `version unknown` (neither the result's header nor the names sidecar of `emir simulate` says the version: never matched to a record, `command` null) with EMIR-W416; `format not covered` (an output format emir verify-sim never writes, such as CSDF: no record can match, `command` null) with EMIR-W464; `records unreadable` (this user may not read the records file: no record counts and none could be kept, `command` null; EMIR-W415 and EMIR-W464). A verification covers kinds of current (`pin_kinds`, one entry per kind the run read: `covered` by the record, `verify_sim_covers` whether any verification of this emir could): a run whose kinds are not all covered is `partly verified` (or `not verified` when none is), `reason` `pin kinds not covered`, with EMIR-W464 naming them; diode, BJT and JFET terminals are never covered. `sim_args` is what the result's names sidecar says the simulator was given (`sim_args_known` false: the result does not say, and it is matched as given none). `ignored_records` counts invalid records, `records_problem` says why a records file cannot be read at all (EMIR-W415).

charts.description: with --html: the run's EM/IR chart, every net on the layout (emir_chart.png, and emir_chart_light.png), absolute paths; empty when it was not drawn (the notices say why: EMIR-I720, EMIR-W720)

anyOf.description: where the item is: [llx, lly, urx, ury] in um (the DSPF's $LLX..$URY, or the layout's rectangle); null when the extraction wrote no coordinates

the grid whose droop is fed back: `RC` when it has capacitance (`caps` capacitors of the DSPF, capacitor devices sized by cap_models included, `caps_F` in all, each to ground; `decaps` MOS decaps, `decaps_F` in all, each behind its access resistance, as --dynamic models them), else `R-only` (EMIR-W544 when the DSPF has no capacitance on the net). `unsized_caps` capacitor devices and `unsized_decaps` MOS decaps the process file cannot size are left out (EMIR-W547: the devices then read low, those decaps' straps are not checked); `simulated_decaps` decaps the testbench simulates (their current loads the grid through their pins)

how the net's branch currents were scored: `RC` through the RC grid (--dynamic's decap-aware EM, `basis` decap-aware); `max(R-only, RC)` per segment the larger of the two (--dynamic, the worst basis: conservative, it keeps the R-only grid's high readings); else `R-only`, the superposition of the pin currents on the R-only grid (EMIR-W545 when `feedback` is RC and the pins' currents vary). `ac`: whether the pins' currents vary over the window (constant ones charge no capacitor: every scoring agrees)
the PWL compression tolerance of the droop this pass simulated (0.3 x the loop's tolerance, coarser when the point cap forced it: EMIR-W542)
the first update's scale: 1, or below it when the plain droop was above 15 % of the supply (`plain (scaled)`)

how far the answer moved from the pass before (relative; null on pass 0): the governing branch's avg, rms and peak; `items`, any item the run reports (its ratio at or above the warning fraction); `devices`, any device's own avg, rms or peak current; `branches`, any branch carrying at least 1 % of the largest (reported, not a stopping condition)

the per-pin device admittance g + C d/dt that computed the droop this pass simulated (the companion update; null for pass 0 and pass 1): [median, max] over the pins, fitted from the two passes before (the secant of current against droop, clipped at >= 0); `frozen`: the fit was kept from an earlier pass (the residual was small)

the split's KCL on this pass: the split pins' currents against the testbench's rail source over the window (`avg_rel`), and at every instant relative to its peak (`instant_rel`); EMIR-W541 above 1e-5 / 1e-4; null where the rail source's current is not saved (Spectre, a ground net)
the DC voltage the testbench drives the net with, read from it (Xyce, ngspice, HSPICE; null volts when it cannot be read): --vdd is checked against it (EMIR-E523)

--self-consistent: every pass of the waveform loop (emir/tdloop.py). Pass 0 is the open-loop cc-grid result. Each pass feeds every pin of the net its own droop waveform (`fed_by`: plain after pass 0, scaled down when it is above 15 % of the supply, the companion update after that). `residual_mV` (also `droop_change_mV`): the largest difference, over the pins and the whole transient, between the droop the pass's currents produce through the grid (`feedback`) and the droop the pass simulated, the PWL as written (pass 0: the open-loop droop); `tolerance_mV`: max(`tol_rel` x the largest droop, `tol_mV`). `converged` (the pass stops the loop; `stop_rule` says by which rule): `residual`, the residual is below the tolerance and the governing branch's avg, rms and peak moved less than 0.5 % (`metric_change`); or `metrics` (`stopped: settled`), on this pass and the one before the governing branch, every reported item and every device moved less than 0.5 %, with the residual under 5 % of the droop, not grown by more than 10 % on either pass, and the PWL not coarsened past the tolerance: the residual then stays above its tolerance. `at_pass_limit`: it converged on the last pass --max-passes allows. `current_change`: the largest change of a branch's average current from the pass before, relative to the largest branch (null on pass 0). `seconds`: the pass's simulation; `post_seconds`: the grid side; `points`: the simulator's time points; `pwl_points`: the PWL points per pin it was fed, one time base for every pin of every net (at most `pwl_cap`: max(1 500, 0.3 x pass 0's time points)). `reported_pass` is the pass the net's results come from: the converged one, or pass 0 (the open loop) when the loop stopped at --max-passes (EMIR-W407), was stopped by its guard (EMIR-W406) or a later pass's simulation ran past its time limit or failed (EMIR-W543); `stopped` says which. `nets`: every net the loop closed together. Each pin's supply is the testbench's rail plus its droop; `vdd` is that rail's voltage (--vdd, or read from the testbench).
an open-loop cc-grid run with --vdd: the IR drop over the supply (EMIR-W520 above about 0.02)

How the tap currents were superposed through the grid, and why (`reason`). Exact, from waveforms: `dense` (the transfer matrix, branches x taps) or `stream` (time chunks, multi-column back-substitution; when the matrix would exceed --max-memory, or the result has fewer than twice as many time samples as taps): the same answer either way. `scalar`: per-tap scalars (--scalars, a tap file with rms and peak, a chip-level run with --align inphase): avg exact, rms and peak in-phase upper bounds. `combined`: a chip-level run with --align async or a phase sweep, per-block rows combined as `reason` says. null for the DC and rcc routes.

The worst dynamic droop on the net and where: rcc from the measured branch currents; cc-grid (--dynamic) from the CC tap waveforms through the RC grid, open loop, or with --self-consistent from the loop's reported pass (each pin fed its droop waveform; `source` says which). null when not computed (a notice says why).

em_basis.description: The EM verdict's basis on this net: `requested` (--em-basis, or the default worst), `used` (the basis the net's verdict, max_ratio, worst, worst_items and governing_metric are on; `measured` in rcc, where the decaps' currents are simulated), `source` (default or option: a basis other than the default is the person's choice, EMIR-W437; no-dynamic: decap-free because the run has neither --dynamic nor --em-basis, EMIR-W428) and, when decap-aware EM was not computed, `fallback` (why, machine-readable; the verdict is then on decap-free) and `fallback_reason` (in words). `decaps_not_sized`: decap devices cap_models cannot size (EMIR-W409, W410), left out of the decap-aware solve: their straps are not checked, and a basis that needs decap-aware EM is not honoured on the net.

anyOf.description: --dynamic in cc-grid: the net's EM from the dynamic solve. `bases`: per basis (decap-free, the static superposition; decap-aware, rms and peak from the dynamic solve with the decaps, avg the static one; worst, per segment the larger) its verdict, worst ratios, governing metric, worst segment and violation count. `higher_aware`: segments at or above the warn fraction that read higher with their decaps than without (what decap-free does not cover). `feed`: the current the feed delivers in both bases. `decaps`: the decaps' own currents (devices, not checked against a metal limit; at most 20). `capacitance`: what the solve counted, and the coupling to signal nets it left out. `items`: the segments of every basis with each basis's own ratio. `numerics`: the step, the passes, the periodic-average check, the step correction of rms, the sub-steps of the waveforms' fast edges. null when not computed (`em_basis.fallback` says why).
The avg limits applied above the temperature they hold at (no jmax_factor table, or above its top): not conservative there

bidirectional.description: Per net, branches whose current reverses: the signed average the avg check uses cancels, while the time average of |I| reaches the warn fraction of the avg limit. EMIR applies no bidirectional (recovery) rule: check them against the PDK's AC rule.

diagonal_wires.description: Per net, the wires on diagonal (non-Manhattan) shapes (`$dir=diag`, the magic route): checked at the width magic gives, its tiles' extent and not the width across the current, so their current density can read low (EMIR-W647).

via_crowding.description: Per net, via arrays within 10 % of the limit: the per-cut check uses the array's mean current, and the cuts facing the current carry more; confirm them cut by cut (the extractor's per-cut vias).

decap_straps_not_covered.description: Per net, the decaps whose straps the EM verdict does not cover: no --dynamic (EMIR-W428), decaps cap_models cannot size (EMIR-W409, W410), the decap-free basis (the segments that read higher with their decaps, EMIR-W436), or decap-aware EM not computed.

shell.description: present (true) when the command is not an emir command (ls, tail, klayout ...): it needs a shell, which the MCP server does not have (emir_cli refuses it with EMIR-E591)

needs_human.description: present (true) when the step leads to a run the person decides on (it re-simulates, or runs a licensed tool): ask them first

items.description: Exact commands to run next, in order; each runs as printed. An emir command keeps the caller's --format, except a run's `emir report` step (its Markdown is what to relay).

hierarchy.description: A run with --abstract: the blocks, the voltage at every block pin, the pass-through inside blocks fed at several pins, the IR budget per block (exact for one pin, an upper bound for several) and the port-voltages file for back-annotation.

em_basis.description: --dynamic or --em-basis (or a net with decap devices on a run without --dynamic: requested decap-free, EMIR-W428): the basis asked for (with --dynamic the default is worst); `used`, the bases the nets' verdicts are on (each net's `em_basis.used`); `honoured` false when a net could not have the basis asked for (`not_computed`: which and why; its verdict is then decap-free, or, for decaps-not-sized, the basis without the decaps cap_models cannot size (`models`); --fail-on-violation exits 1)

cwd.description: the directory the run ran in: the relative paths of `argv` are relative to it (`emir next --run-summary` resolves them, so its re-run commands work from any directory)

anyOf.description: Where the limits the run applied came from: the process file's `provenance` (null: not stated), and per layer and via in use its own provenance, the source (document, table or page) of each value, the values a hand-entered file gives with no source (EMIR-W320), its EM limit keys and its width loss (and, on a --dynamic run, the cap models: kind `cap`); the temperature the limits hold at, their derating and the temperatures with no source (`temperature.unsourced`); and `suspects`: the values outside the range their quantity normally takes, most often a unit slip (EMIR-W321; `blocking`: the input check refuses them, EMIR-E331; `confirmed`: listed under the file's `unit_confirmed`).
